item.title: STORY | CAPF Act that governs officer posts, deputation comes into force The Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Act, 2026, which pro...
item.description:
STORY | CAPF Act that governs officer posts, deputation comes into force

The Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Act, 2026, which provides a common framework for recruitment and conditions of service of Group-A general duty officers and other officers in the CAPFs, came into force on Thursday, according to a government notification.

The notification came at a time when the Supreme Court is hearing a bunch of petitions filed by thousands of CAPF officers challenging the validity of the law that was passed by the Parliament in April.

"In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (2) of section 1 of the Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Act, 2026, the Central Government hereby appoints the 08th day of October, 2026, as the date on which the provisions of the said Act shall come into force," said the notification issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs.

The CAPF Act provides for regulation of recruitment, promotion, deputation and other conditions of service of officers in the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), Border Security Force (BSF), Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) and Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB).

item.title: 🇲🇽 MEXICO: THREAT ACTOR CLAIMS DATABASE OF 18,000 DOCTORS FROM MEDICAL SPECIALTY CERTIFICATION BODY CONACEM A threat actor on an underground for...
item.description:
🇲🇽 MEXICO: THREAT ACTOR CLAIMS DATABASE OF 18,000 DOCTORS FROM MEDICAL SPECIALTY CERTIFICATION BODY CONACEM

A threat actor on an underground forum has posted what they claim is a database of about 18,000 doctors from CONACEM, the committee that oversees certification of medical specialists in Mexico and acts as an auxiliary body of the federal public administration.

The listing claims:
* About 18,000 doctor records
* Full names (first name and both surnames), sex, date of birth, nationality, country and state of birth
* Personal phone numbers, professional licence numbers (cédula profesional) and RFC tax IDs
* Title and user IDs from the certification system

The claim has not been independently verified.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
The capture shows a column list only, with no sample rows. The fields match what a specialist certification registry would hold, and the mix of RFC tax IDs, licence numbers, birth dates and private phone numbers would be enough to impersonate doctors or target them with extortion and fake-regulator calls, which are common in Mexico. This is an unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation that CONACEM was breached. Doctors certified through CONACEM should be wary of calls or emails about their certification or licence.

#DDW #DarkWeb #Mexico #CONACEM #Healthcare #Government #DataBreach #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

item.description:

Prosecutors allege he obtained roughly 2,000 intelligence documents, many classified, through a former senior BND aide. Investigators are examining whether any of it was passed to Chinese intelligence operatives, and are reviewing his years-long relationship with Chinese Major General Wang Jianzheng, a former military attaché in Germany.

Hanning denies wrongdoing. German media reports.

item.title: 🇪🇹 ETHIOPIA: THREAT ACTOR CLAIMS MINISTRY OF HEALTH DATABASE, 65GB HEALTH INFORMATION SYSTEM BACKUP OFFERED A threat actor on an underground for...
item.description:
🇪🇹 ETHIOPIA: THREAT ACTOR CLAIMS MINISTRY OF HEALTH DATABASE, 65GB HEALTH INFORMATION SYSTEM BACKUP OFFERED

A threat actor on an underground forum is offering a free download of what they claim is data from Ethiopia's federal Ministry of Health.

The listing claims:
* "hmis_custom_backup.dump", a 6GB PostgreSQL backup said to expand to 65GB once restored
* Or "dhis_database.zip", a 0.5GB archive said to expand to 6GB of cleaned CSV tables
* A defacement-style banner image, a donation request and a hint that more is coming

The claim has not been independently verified.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
The file names point to the ministry's Health Management Information System (HMIS), which in Ethiopia runs on the DHIS2 platform used to collect facility-level health reporting. DHIS2 data is often aggregate statistics rather than individual patient records, but backups can also hold user accounts, staff details and some patient-level tracker data. The capture shows no table list or sample rows, so the contents cannot be checked. This is an unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation that Ethiopia's Ministry of Health was breached.

#DDW #DarkWeb #Ethiopia #Healthcare #Government #DataBreach #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity
